first.rationale: Onboarding completion is down 4% QoQ, creating immediate friction for new accounts. Memory_31 and memory_86 directly demonstrated that signup simplification and shortened onboarding drive activation lift. These are the most directly causative levers for the current activation decline. Verifying these two memories reduces execution risk on what appears to be our highest-confidence intervention. While promotional_pricing (memory_73) addresses competitive pressure, it risks long-term unit economics and creates unsustainable revenue. referral_incentive (memory_57) applies to established customers, not the new-account activation problem. enterprise_sales_assist (memory_44) doesn't solve the SMB activation decline. A simplified onboarding experiment this week can deliver quick signal on whether the 4% activation drop is friction-driven, and aligns with our primary objective of sustainable revenue by improving both conversion efficiency and early product adoption. The uncertainty around magnitude of impact is preserved—we will run a standard experiment to validate at current scale before broad rollout.

final.rationale: Archive verification confirms both memories with strong evidence. Memory_31 showed +9% activation and +4% qualified revenue lift on SMB signup simplification, with only -1% retention risk. Memory_86 showed +13% completion lift, -2.1 day time-to-value improvement, and +3% retention benefit from shortened onboarding. Combined, these demonstrate that friction reduction in early user flows directly addresses our current activation decline (down 6% QoQ). The onboarding completion drop (down 4% QoQ) aligns precisely with memory_86's lever. Signup simplification further reduces early abandonment. Both interventions preserve 30-day retention or improve it, protecting sustainable revenue. Promotional pricing would undermine unit economics against our primary objective. This standard experiment will generate fast signal (week 1-2) on whether friction is the activation driver, positioning us to scale if validated. The 4% qualified revenue upside from memory_31 plus retention protection from memory_86 compounds toward long-term value.
